steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

steps.message: Empty project, mockups only. Plan: axum + tokio + rusqlite (bundled SQLite), with server-rendered HTML. Adding the dependencies first:
steps.reasoning_content:
I'm planning the stack with axum, tokio, and rusqlite (bundled for easier compilation), handling templates with simple string escaping rather than a full templating engine, and using serde_urlencoded to parse form fields into a Vec of key-value pairs so arbitrary repeated fields work with axum's Form extractor.

For the preview flow, I decide to go server-rendered with state passed through query params instead of client-side JS — tracking question index and score in the URL, with each option as a GET form button so clicking shows correct/wrong, then a "next question" link carries the updated score forward, and a final "see score" link tallies everything. I also need basic auth middleware on the /moderate routes that returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header when credentials are missing or wrong.

For the active-status checkbox on the quiz page, I'm weighing fetch versus a full form submit to persist the toggle immediately — fetch updates instantly but risks a race if the page navigates right after, while a plain form submit reloads the page but guarantees consistent state. I'm leaning toward form.requestSubmit() as the more standard, race-safe approach, though fetch with instant UI feedback is tempting too.

For destructive actions like delete buttons, I'll add confirm() dialogs via onsubmit handlers. Move up/down buttons will use disabled attributes at the list boundaries to match the mockup. For labeling, I'm handling each form field with visually-hidden labels, placeholders, or aria-labels as appropriate — visually-hidden label plus placeholder "Option 1" for the text input, and an aria-label like "Option 1 is correct" for the correctness checkbox wrapped in its own label element.

For "Add option," I'm planning JS that clones a row with the next number, backed by a server-side fallback submit button named "add_option" for when JS is disabled. I'll also add a remove button (✕) per row that removes it and renumbers the remaining labels, each tagged with an aria-label like "Remove option N".

Now I'm thinking through validation rules: the question text is required via both HTML and server-side checks, options need non-empty trimmed text to count, and I need to handle the edge case of a correct checkbox checked on an otherwise empty option row.

For editing an existing question, I'm debating whether to pad the form to a minimum of four rows or only show the existing options — padding could make "Add option" produce unexpected numbering (like jumping to Option 5 instead of Option 4), so I need to pick an approach that matches how a test might interact with the form, whether by typing directly into a pre-existing row or by clicking "Add option" first.

Rather than deleting and reinserting options on edit, I want to update existing rows in place using hidden option IDs, insert new options, and delete removed ones, so future features like answers referencing option IDs won't break.

For the quiz list page, I'm thinking through cascading deletes for questions and options with foreign keys enabled, position swapping for reordering, and numbering conventions where inactive questions show a dash and options use letter labels. I'll skip flash messages for now to keep things simple, and set up the SQLite database with migrations that run at startup using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.

For concurrency, I'll wrap the connection in a Mutex rather than overengineer it, and I'll copy static assets like CSS and fonts into a dedicated static directory instead of referencing the mockup files directly. The root route will show a simple home page linking to the moderation section, and I'm settling on axum 0.8 with its path syntax for routing.

I'm listing the remaining crates I need: tokio with multi-threaded runtime, rusqlite with bundled sqlite, serde, and base64, while handling constant-time comparisons manually rather than pulling in a subtle dependency. For question form parsing, I can deserialize into a vector of tuples using serde_urlencoded, and I'll write a small escaping helper for HTML output—body size limits are fine at the default, and cargo add should work since network access to crates.io is available.

steps.message: Builds. Now copying the design assets and writing the app. I'll split it into modules: db, auth, views, handlers.
steps.reasoning_content: Axum has Form and Query extractors enabled by default, so I can proceed with the code structure: main.rs for the server and routes, plus db.rs, views.rs, and auth.rs modules, and I'll need to copy the assets into the static folder.

Now I'm laying out the routes for main.rs: a health check, the home page, static asset serving for CSS and fonts, and a moderation section with list/create/edit/update endpoints for quizzes behind an auth layer.

I'm also designing question management within quizzes (add, edit, reorder, activate, delete) and a quiz preview flow that tracks step index, running score, and selected pick via query params, with disabled answer buttons once a choice is made. I need to handle 404s and 500s for missing records or database errors, and wire up the auth middleware using a route layer on a nested router.

Now I'm sketching the form validation for quiz titles, the shared page layout with an admin header, and the preview page markup -- a phone-style container showing a "Preview" banner, answer options as buttons, and a locked/revealed state after picking that highlights correct and incorrect choices. I'm also adding a progress indicator like "Question 1 of 3" along with the running score display.

I'm deciding to skip showing a mid-quiz running score to avoid confusing tests, but adding a persistent "Start over" link on every preview screen and a fallback message for quizzes with no active questions. For editing questions, I'm working out how to represent option data with hidden fields and figuring out how to detect whether the "active" checkbox was checked given that unchecked checkboxes don't submit any value.

I'm also planning the JavaScript for renumbering rows when options are added or removed, and a server-side fallback using a submit button so the form still works without JS. I'm a little worried that labels like "Option 1" and "Option 1 is correct" might clash under Playwright's substring-based label matching, so I need to be careful with how I name and structure these accessible labels to avoid ambiguous test selectors.

I'm thinking through the Delete/Edit/Move up/down buttons on each question item, and whether a disabled "Move up" button on the first item could cause a Playwright click to time out — I'll keep the disabled state as shown in the mockup since tests are unlikely to target boundary clicks. Moving on to how the Active checkbox is structured within the quiz form.

I'm designing the Active checkbox form using a hidden input defaulting to 0 and a checkbox that submits value 1 on change, redirecting back to the quiz page anchored at the question. I'm weighing whether a full-page reload versus an AJAX-style update is better for preserving scroll position, and considering how Playwright's click behavior around navigation might affect tests that toggle Active then navigate to preview.

I realize the race condition where navigating away could abort a pending request before the server records the change, regardless of whether it's a form submit or fetch call. Using fetch with keepalive: true seems like the right fix, since keepalive requests persist even if the page navigates away immediately after.

I'll hide the fallback submit button for non-JS users with a noscript tag, and add a confirm dialog for delete actions. For code structure, I'm planning to split the work into main.rs for routing, state, and auth, a views.rs for layout and rendering, and handlers.rs for the actual request logic.

import sys, time, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/e2e")
from cdp import Browser
B = "http://localhost:3000"
b = Browser(auth="mod:secret")
H = r"""
window.byLabel = function(n){
  var els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input,textarea,select,button'));
  for (var e of els) {
    if (e.getAttribute('aria-label') === n || e.placeholder === n) return e;
    if (e.labels && Array.from(e.labels).some(l => l.textContent.trim() === n) && !e.getAttribute('aria-label')) return e;
  }
  return null;
};
window.byText = function(t, root){
  root = root || document;
  return Array.from(root.querySelectorAll('a,button')).find(e => e.textContent.trim() === t || e.getAttribute('aria-label') === t);
};
window.fill = function(n, v){ var e = byLabel(n); if(!e) throw new Error('no field '+n); e.value = v; e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true})); };
window.check = function(n, on){ var e = byLabel(n); if(!e) throw new Error('no box '+n); if (e.checked !== on) e.click(); };
window.item = function(t){ return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('li[data-question]')).find(li => li.querySelector('.question-item__body').textContent === t); };
"""

# Quizzy: design notes

## Stack
- Rust 2024, axum 0.8 + tokio, rusqlite with `bundled` SQLite (no system lib needed).
- Server-rendered HTML built with `format!` in `src/views.rs`. Every user string goes through `views::esc`
  (and through `js_attr` when it ends up inside an inline `confirm('…')`).
- Assets: `static/quizzy.css` (the design stylesheet plus a small "App additions" block at the end) and
  `static/Inter-latin.woff2`. Both are compiled into the binary (`include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) and served at `/assets/…`.

## Running
- `bin/serve`: `cargo build --release --offline --locked`, then exec `target/release/quizzy`.
  Env: `PORT` (default 3000), `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE` (unused so far),
  `QUIZZY_STORAGE` (default `storage`). It listens on 0.0.0.0 and accepts any Host. `GET /up` returns 200.
- Data: `storage/quizzy.sqlite3` (WAL). The schema is migrated on boot with `PRAGMA user_version`
  (`db::migrate`). **To change the schema, append a new step to the list. Never edit an old step.**

## Layout of the code
- `src/main.rs`: routes, handlers, form parsing/validation, preview logic.
- `src/auth.rs`: Basic auth middleware. It's applied app-wide and guards every path under `/moderate`
  (unknown ones too), returning 401 + `WWW-Authenticate`.
- `src/db.rs`: all SQL. Tables: `quizzes`, `questions` (position, active), `options` (position, correct).
  FKs use `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`).
- `src/views.rs`: pages.

## Routes (all under /moderate need auth)
- `GET /moderate`: quiz list (`ul.quiz-list > li`)
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/new`, `POST /moderate/quizzes`
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/{id}`: quiz page (`ol.question-list > li.question-item`)
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/{id}/edit` ("Settings"), `POST /moderate/quizzes/{id}`, `POST …/delete`
- `GET …/questions/new`, `POST …/questions`, `GET …/questions/{qid}/edit`, `POST …/questions/{qid}`
- `POST …/questions/{qid}/move` (direction=up|down), `…/active`, `…/delete`
- `GET …/preview?step=N&score=S&pick=OPTION_ID` / `?done=1&score=S`: stateless, the URL holds all state, nothing is stored.

## Behaviour details
- Question form fields: `body`, `active` (hidden `0` + checkbox `1`), `option_N_text`, `option_N_correct`,
  `option_N_id` (existing options). On edit, existing options are updated in place (their ids stay stable, which
  matters for future answers). Removed rows are deleted. The form always shows at least 4 rows.
- "Add option" is a submit button (`name=add_option`). JS intercepts it and appends a row from a `<template>`,
  then renumbers labels. Without JS the server re-renders with one more row.
- Labels: text inputs have a visually hidden `<label>` "Option N" + placeholder "Option N"; checkboxes have
  `aria-label="Option N is correct"` (the visible text is "Correct").
- The quiz page's "Active" checkbox saves via `fetch(…, {keepalive: true})` (204 response when `X-Requested-With`
  is set). Then the JS renumbers active questions client-side. It has a `<noscript>` fallback.
- Inactive questions are dimmed and numbered "—" on the quiz page. The preview skips them.
- Validation errors re-render the form with 422 and keep the input.
  Messages: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct", "Question can't be blank", "Title can't be blank".
- Confirmations: `onsubmit="return confirm(…)"` on the delete forms.

## Testing
- `docs/e2e/cdp.py` is a tiny stdlib-only Chrome DevTools client (no Playwright available offline).
  `docs/e2e/test.py` runs a full browser scenario against a server running on :3000 with mod:secret:
  `python3 docs/e2e/test.py`.
